messages:
maria: Heads-up — thinking of adding a persistent correlation-id into sampled request/response logs so we can join telemetry, traces, and console audit slices. Concern: does that create an easy PII re-identification vector?

arjun: +1 on the usefulness. main risk is if the correlation-id can be mapped back to a user identifier stored elsewhere. we should treat it like sensitive metadata.

sophia: what if we never log the raw ID but only a salted hash? e.g. store `X-Corr: sha256(id + tenant_salt)` so it is stable for the tenant but not globally linkable.

liam: salted-hash is decent, but if support needs to link a specific request to a user for debugging, how do we reconcile? we could offer an opt-in decrypt path via KMS with strict audit + short TTL.

maria: agree. design sketch:
```
headers captured: { "x-correlation-id": "<raw>" } // capture at edge
ingest step: derive hashed_id = HMAC(tenant_salt, raw) // one-way
store: hashed_id in logs + sampling metadata + consent_flag
```
Only allow raw->user lookup via a hotel key that requires 2-person approval and is logged.

arjun: also important to honor telemetry consent per-route. if `telemetry_consent=opt_out` we must drop the correlation-id entirely (no hash). Otherwise hashing still could be considered telemetry depending on legal.

sophia: console UX thinking: show a trace link based on hashed_id but mark it as "hashed" and show a per-tenant toggle: "Allow support mapping (audited)". default = off.

liam: storage/analytics implications: third-party sinks (datadog/bigquery) will receive hashed_id. we need to advise customers and add a pipeline flag to redact hashed_id before external export if tenant requests it.

maria: good call. add `export_redact_policy` per-tenant + global default. Also retention: hashed_id should be TTL'd at 30 days by default. increase only via explicit contract.

devex-bot: FYI: customer-facing docs will need a short note on what correlation-id means, how to opt-in/out, and what the support mapping process looks like.

arjun: security note: HMAC is preferable to raw SHA256 to avoid preimage rainbow attacks; tenant_salt must be rotated periodically and stored in KMS. rotation strategy: generate new salt -> start writing new hashed_ids with version tag -> keep old mapping for 7 days for consistency.

liam: rollout proposal: canary at 0.5% traffic for internal tenants with explicit consent flag set, run for 2 weeks, collect telemetry on false-positive user mapping attempts and memory/cost delta. then expand.

maria: ops question — what about sampled responses with user-supplied content? we must still scrub any user PII from request/response bodies. correlation-id + hashed link should never reintroduce raw PII.

sophia: agreed. enforce body scrubber in the same pipeline stage before correlation hashing is appended to the event.

ops-bot: deploy: started canary job `corr-id-canary` at 0.5% for staging. Build: infra/corr-id-v1. ETA: 10m.

liam: small nit — include a header `x-corr-version: v1` so we can evolve scheme safely. also add `x-telemetry-consent: opt_in|opt_out` to incoming requests to make decision deterministic.

maria: action items: 1) arjun to draft KMS-based salt + rotation plan (PR by EOD Thu). 2) sophia to prototype hashing + header flags in edge lambda (PR next week). 3) devex to draft doc blurb and support mapping playbook. 4) ops to monitor canary and abort on any sign of leak.

arjun: noted. will also include a sample policy snippet for export redaction.

maria: thanks all. if nobody objects we'll start blocking off the canary and legal review this afternoon. :thumbsup:
